title: Acid–Base–Buffer Properties and Chemical Properties of Food
shortDescription: pH, buffering, and the reactions (browning, oxidation, hydrolysis) that change food chemistry.
genZNote: pH decides what grows, what sets and what tastes sour. Maillard vs caramelisation is the classic trap — one needs amino acids, one just needs heat and sugar.

sections.heading: Acidity, pH and Buffers
bullets: pH = −log[H+]; food classes: low-acid (pH > 4.6), acid (pH ≤ 4.6) — 4.6 is the critical boundary for C. botulinum spore germination in canning.
Buffer = weak acid + conjugate base resisting pH change (Henderson–Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log [A−]/[HA]). Food buffers: citrate, phosphate, lactate, proteins (milk buffers at pH 6.6–6.8).
Titratable acidity (as lactic/citric acid) differs from pH; both are measured in dairy and juices.
Applications: curdling at pH 4.6 (casein), pectin gel at pH ~3.0–3.5, leavening agents (baking soda + acid), acidification as a hurdle.
Typical pH: lemon 2.2–2.4; tomato ~4.3; milk 6.6–6.8; egg white 7.6→9.2 on ageing; meat post-rigor 5.4–5.6.

sections.heading: Chemical Properties and Reactions
sections.body: Pigments: chlorophyll (green), carotenoids (orange-yellow; provitamin A), anthocyanins (red-blue), flavonoids and betalains (beetroot). Flavour compounds arise from reactions among sugars, amino acids and lipids.

table.caption: Key reactions
rows: Cut apples/potatoes; stop with acid, blanching, antioxidants
Chlorophyll → pheophytin (olive green); anthocyanins pH-sensitive; carotenoids stable

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: pH and buffering govern microbial safety, protein functionality and sensory quality, while Maillard, oxidative and enzymatic reactions drive chemical change in foods.
keyFacts: Maillard needs reducing sugar + amino group.

commonTraps: Do not confuse Maillard (needs amino acids) with caramelisation (sugar only).

questions.prompt: Foods with pH below 4.6 are classified as:
Browning that needs amino groups and reducing sugars is:
questions.explanation: Maillard involves amines and reducing sugars.

questions.prompt: Milk resists pH change mainly because of:
questions.explanation: Casein, whey proteins and phosphate buffer milk.
